WHAT A NODE ADD/REMOVE ACTUALLY CHANGES

decommissioned (in-flight tasks flushed first) on scale-down
Bursty / spiky job with idle gaps?
Keep decommission.enabled = true (default) so idle nodes release fast and billing stops.
Job has repeated short lulls between stages?
Set decommission.enabled = false to avoid scale-down/scale-up thrash between stages.
Raise the pool's configured max — autoscale still won't exceed it mid-job.
Note: resizing node SIZE (not count) still forces a session restart either way.
COLD-START AND BILLING CONTEXT FOR SCALING EVENTS
new worker joins existing head node
Billed window: only while a session actively executes — idle pre-warm, acquisition, and post-job deallocation are unbilled for every scale-up/scale-down event above.
Fixed bound (does not change with load)

g.title: Spark job demand — A notebook or Spark Job Definition submits work against a configured pool.
Minimum executor reserve — Dynamic allocation reserves executors from the pool minimum at submission.
Tasks exceed capacity? — Dynamic allocation grows executors when runnable tasks outstrip capacity.
Scale toward maximum — The pool adds workers only within its configured maximum.
Idle executors detected? — Executors become release candidates after work completes or idles.
Decommission safely — Fabric enables executor decommission by default for automatic scale-down.
Shuffle blocks pin workers — Local shuffle data can prevent release until downstream readers finish.
